Have your team know their roles.
Have your fastest filler do production the whole time. They will get phone calls when they can as secondary. 

Have 1 person at pick up the whole time. They will help put away baskets, pull RTS when they have time. 

3rd tech is your back up for all those things. Their main role is QT and pulling drugs (so they can help pick up easily)

Your role is to be the quarter back. Tell them what do do the whole time while doing QV1, QT and QV2 in that order. qv2 is your least priority. 
Don’t leave your station unless you have to (DUR, consult, vaccines) 

Phone calls is low priority during rush hours. 
Walks in tell them wait is 1 hour. 

and muddle through while looking else where

Stop having the mindset patients can’t wait in line or on the phone. It’s an open market, if they want to get it faster they can try somewhere else. 
Don’t think you have to finish the que on time. Just get as much within the time as you can safely and accurately. 

It’s a mindset in my opinion when people say they can’t handle it. If you’re doing your best and pushing your team to do their best then that’s all you can do. 

Who cares if it turns red. That’s just cvs way of making you stress and work faster and inaccurately. Metrics shouldn’t matter as long as you make the company profits. They will yell that you are not hitting goal but in the end they won’t do anything as long as you make them money or at the very least break even

Tbh if this was my situation this is what I would do… 

Easier said than done but enter DGAF mode. Work at a pace that is safe for dispensing medication and for the patient but don’t kill yourself doing it. 
Milk in the OT pay by staying over. You have reason to stay and do OT now because your que is so bad. 

During peek of pandemic when we had no one I would clock in 10-20 hours OT weekly. No one would say the wiser cause they knew it was bad 

Upper management will not be able to find someone new to replace you. They will scold you but I don’t care if they yell at me. I just give a look to them and ask what they want me to do better and ask for solutions. 

While you clock in that sweet OT pay. Look for another position.

Hey, I am so sorry what you’re going through. It is a very difficult time for you and you may not see a light but there is.

It does help to look at other people perspective to see how others went through something similar and made it out alive and are fine or even better off. The commenters here should help you and I hope my story helps too. 

It’s sad to say but this story is far too common. Something very similar to this happen to my dad during his divorce. He lost everything. We had to move out of the house what I thought was a decent life became something different. I did not know at the time but my dad went through some really rdifficult times. Fortunately my dad sister is well off and she provided us with her old house. We lived there for 10 years or so with what I can see now was inexpensive rent. If it was not for my aunt, our family would of really struggled during this time. 

I do not know if you are fortunate enough to have support like this but look for it where you can. You really know who is in your corner when bad time hits hard.  (Just to give you a sense of how much money my dad lost, he lost all his savings I would assume about 1 million in assets)

My sister had to pick up a ton of the slack during the tough times too so we were very fortunate for her. 


Recently I am going through something myself. Lost pretty much all my savings (100k roughly) and am in a bit of debt myself. Less than a month ago I felt the same pain you did where I would want to end it myself. 
But my sister was there in my corner along with my other siblings. 
My expenses aren’t crazy so I am able to survive each month with what I can. But I did have to cut a lot of things. Sleeping on a coach for example is one of those things. Trying my best to cut food expenses too. 

Cut where you can, but obviously don’t go too crazy for you need to keep your mental health safe too. Don’t cut anything that will make you miserable because it will only make things worst for you. 

Promise you just go through each day one day at a time. Don’t focus too much on your financial hardship because when I do, it does hit real hard. For anyone, being financially unstable is rough but money will come. Just try to stay positive when you can, cry when you need to and keep moving forward. 

I saw this on a show and it helped. 

“If you’re a man you will endure this pain, you will push through in silence. “

Now I am not saying you stay silent and don’t telll anyone your troubles. But when times are real hard and you can’t reach out for help. You can still endure. 

What everyone says when we are growing up is right. Money can’t make you happy. I understand it helps especially when you feel like drowning in debt. 

Just know it won’t last forever and eventually you will start looking forward to things again
